cleanIntro: This guide follows Benelli's manual for the Lupo bolt-action rifle family, which never prints the Lupo or HPR name, so check your variant against it. The bolt comes out of the upper receiver at the press of a side button, and its cap and striker unit come out of the bolt. The upper receiver sits on a chassis, held by two screws. The routine strip takes the bolt out; Deep Clean takes the striker out of the bolt and separates the magazine, the upper receiver and the trigger group, and there Benelli says the rifle is completely stripped.

steps.title: Safety on — the red dot must disappear
steps.action: This guide follows Benelli's manual for the Lupo family, which does not print the Lupo HPR name, so check your variant against it. Slide the safety button on the cover back until the red dot on the upper receiver is no longer visible.
steps.prose: Benelli defines safe by what you cannot see: the red dot means firing position. The book asks for every stripping and maintenance step to be done with the safety on, so it stays on for the whole guide.
steps.quote: Engage the safety by sliding back the button on the cover
steps.cite: Use • Maintenance — Benelli bolt-action rifle (served by Benelli USA as the Lupo manual, listed for the Lupo HPR) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Use — Safety, p.23
steps.warn: All assembly/stripping and maintenance operations must only be performed with the SAFETY ENGAGED.

steps.title: Bolt locking lever? Press it to open the bolt
steps.action: Only if your rifle has a bolt locking lever: with the safety on, the bolt is locked closed. To open it, press the bolt locking lever and turn the bolt handle at the same time. A rifle without the lever opens with the handle alone.
steps.prose: The lever is listed as fitted to some rifles only. If the handle will not lift with the safety on, look for it before forcing anything.
steps.quote: To open the bolt, press the bolt locking lever and turn the bolt handle at the same time.
steps.cite: Use • Maintenance — Benelli bolt-action rifle (served by Benelli USA as the Lupo manual, listed for the Lupo HPR) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Use — Bolt locking lever (if equipped on the rifle), p.24

steps.title: Magazine out, then the chambered round ejected
steps.action: With the safety on and the muzzle in a safe direction, release the magazine and take it out. Then open the bolt and draw it back: the round in the chamber is extracted and thrown clear.
steps.prose: Magazine first, so that closing the bolt again cannot feed another round into the chamber.
steps.quote: Open the bolt (a-b): the chambered cartridge will be extracted and ejected.
steps.cite: Use • Maintenance — Benelli bolt-action rifle (served by Benelli USA as the Lupo manual, listed for the Lupo HPR) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Unloading the rifle, steps 1-2, p.26

steps.title: Chamber checked empty, magazine emptied
steps.action: Look into the chamber and confirm it is empty, then close the bolt. Push the cartridges out of the magazine forward, one at a time, and put the empty magazine back in the rifle.
steps.prose: Benelli prints the same line at the head of the stripping section: chamber and magazine both completely empty before the rifle is handled in any way.
steps.aside: Remove the cartridges from the magazine, pushing them forwards (a), then re-insert the empty magazine into the rifle (b).
steps.quote: Verify empty chamber and close bolt.
steps.cite: Use • Maintenance — Benelli bolt-action rifle (served by Benelli USA as the Lupo manual, listed for the Lupo HPR) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Unloading the rifle, steps 3-4, p.26

steps.title: Bolt open, back, side button pressed — bolt out
steps.action: Open the bolt and draw it back. Press the side button on the upper receiver and slide the bolt the rest of the way out of the back.
steps.prose: The side button is the bolt stop. Nothing else holds the bolt in, so there is no tool and no force in this step.
steps.quote: Open the bolt (a) and move it back (b) before pressing the side button on the upper receiver (c) to remove it from the upper receiver itself.
steps.cite: Use • Maintenance — Benelli bolt-action rifle (served by Benelli USA as the Lupo manual, listed for the Lupo HPR) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Stripping procedure, step 1, p.26

steps.title: Medium or high comb? Turn the bolt 180° to clear it
steps.action: If your stock carries a medium or high comb, the bolt will not slide straight out past it. Turn the bolt 180° from its closed position and it comes out without taking the comb off.
steps.prose: The same turn puts the bolt back in. A bolt that stops against the comb is not jammed; it is the wrong way up.
steps.quote: (starting from the closed position) to slide it out from the upper receiver without needing to remove the comb.
steps.cite: Use • Maintenance — Benelli bolt-action rifle (served by Benelli USA as the Lupo manual, listed for the Lupo HPR) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Stripping procedure, note to step 1, p.27

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You have the bolt unit out of the upper receiver and the empty magazine checked. That is what a routine clean needs. Deep Clean carries on with Benelli's same procedure: the bolt cap and striker unit out of the bolt, then the magazine, the upper receiver and the trigger group off the chassis.
steps.prose: Benelli asks for very little: the barrel after use, and the bolt, trigger group and magazine regularly.
steps.quote: Due to the extremely simple construction and to the carefully selected materials, the rifle does not require specific maintenance interventions.
steps.cite: Use • Maintenance — Benelli bolt-action rifle (served by Benelli USA as the Lupo manual, listed for the Lupo HPR) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Maintenance, p.28

steps.title: Barrel cleaned after use
steps.action: Clean the bore after every outing, working from the breech with the bolt out.
steps.prose: This is the first item on Benelli's list and the only one it asks for every time.
steps.quote: routine cleaning of the barrel after use;
steps.cite: Use • Maintenance — Benelli bolt-action rifle (served by Benelli USA as the Lupo manual, listed for the Lupo HPR) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Maintenance, item 1, p.28

steps.title: Bolt unit cleaned and lubricated
steps.action: Wipe the powder residue off the bolt body and its locking surfaces, then oil lightly. Benelli's list says to strip the bolt unit for this — Deep Clean takes the bolt cap and striker unit out.
steps.prose: The same residue that reaches the trigger group reaches the bolt, which is why Benelli names it separately.
steps.quote: Strip, clean and lubricate the bolt unit,
steps.cite: Use • Maintenance — Benelli bolt-action rifle (served by Benelli USA as the Lupo manual, listed for the Lupo HPR) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Maintenance, item 3, p.28

steps.title: Trigger group and magazine kept free of residue
steps.action: Brush powder residue and anything foreign out of the trigger area and the magazine, then oil lightly.
steps.prose: The book's word is regular, not every time. Deep Clean separates the trigger group from the upper receiver if you need to reach it.
steps.quote: regular cleaning and lubrication to remove any powder residues (or foreign bodies) from the trigger group and magazine;
steps.cite: Use • Maintenance — Benelli bolt-action rifle (served by Benelli USA as the Lupo manual, listed for the Lupo HPR) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Maintenance, item 2, p.28

steps.title: Exposed metal oiled; stock and fore-end with their own products
steps.action: Keep a light coat of oil on the parts that weather reaches. Clean the stock and fore-end with products made for their finish, and keep solvent-bearing oils off them.
steps.prose: Benelli warns that oils containing solvents or chemicals can lift or alter the finish on wood, technopolymer, camouflage or varnished parts.
steps.aside: To lubricate and protect the mechanical parts, we recommend using Benelli oil (provided).
steps.quote: to keep the rifle correctly, we recommend keeping any parts subject to the elements lubricated.
steps.cite: Use • Maintenance — Benelli bolt-action rifle (served by Benelli USA as the Lupo manual, listed for the Lupo HPR) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Maintenance, item 4, p.28

deepSteps.title: Bolt cap off — clockwise, side button pressed
deepSteps.action: Hold the bolt unit, press the side button and at the same time turn the bolt cap clockwise, the way the arrow on the cap shows, until it comes free.
deepSteps.prose: The cap is under spring load from the striker. Turn it the way the arrow says — the next step is the recovery if you went the other way.
deepSteps.quote: To remove the bolt cap, turn it clockwise, as shown by the arrow on the cap itself, and press the side button at the same time.
deepSteps.cite: Use • Maintenance — Benelli bolt-action rifle (served by Benelli USA as the Lupo manual, listed for the Lupo HPR) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Stripping procedure, step 2, p.27

deepSteps.title: Turned it the wrong way? Reset it in the receiver
deepSteps.action: If the cap was turned anticlockwise, put the bolt unit upside down into the guides on the upper receiver and turn it back to where it started, then try clockwise again.
deepSteps.prose: Benelli gives the fix because it is an easy mistake. The receiver guides hold the bolt while you turn the cap back.
deepSteps.quote: If turned the wrong way (anticlockwise), insert the upturned bolt unit into the guides on the upper receiver and turn it back to the original position.
deepSteps.cite: Use • Maintenance — Benelli bolt-action rifle (served by Benelli USA as the Lupo manual, listed for the Lupo HPR) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Stripping procedure, note to step 2, p.27

deepSteps.title: Striker unit out of the bolt cap
deepSteps.action: Slide the striker unit out of the bolt cap.
deepSteps.prose: The book's assembly section calls it the firing pin group. Keep it with the cap: they go back together first.
deepSteps.quote: Slide the striker unit out of the bolt cap.
deepSteps.cite: Use • Maintenance — Benelli bolt-action rifle (served by Benelli USA as the Lupo manual, listed for the Lupo HPR) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Stripping procedure, step 3, p.27

deepSteps.title: Magazine released with its lever
deepSteps.action: Press the magazine release lever and take the magazine out of the chassis.
deepSteps.prose: It has to be out before the upper receiver can come off.
deepSteps.quote: Release the magazine (a-b), using the lever.
deepSteps.cite: Use • Maintenance — Benelli bolt-action rifle (served by Benelli USA as the Lupo manual, listed for the Lupo HPR) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Stripping procedure, step 4, p.27

deepSteps.title: Two screws out, upper receiver off the chassis
deepSteps.action: Loosen the two fastening screws with the wrench supplied with the rifle and lift the upper receiver off the chassis.
deepSteps.prose: These are the action screws. They go back to a torque Benelli prints, in a set order, so note which is front and which is back.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the upper receiver by loosening the two fastening screws with the wrench provided.
deepSteps.cite: Use • Maintenance — Benelli bolt-action rifle (served by Benelli USA as the Lupo manual, listed for the Lupo HPR) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Stripping procedure, step 5, p.27

deepSteps.title: Trigger group off the upper receiver
deepSteps.action: Take out the two fastening screws on the sides and remove the trigger group from the upper receiver.
deepSteps.prose: Clean the trigger group as a unit. The book gives no procedure for taking it further apart.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the trigger group (a-b) from the upper receiver, using the two fastening screws on the sides.
deepSteps.cite: Use • Maintenance — Benelli bolt-action rifle (served by Benelli USA as the Lupo manual, listed for the Lupo HPR) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Stripping procedure, step 6, p.27

deepSteps.title: Bolt stop pin still in place — completely stripped
deepSteps.action: Check that the fastening pin on the bolt stop has stayed where it belongs now that the upper receiver is off. Benelli says this is the end: the rifle is completely stripped.
deepSteps.prose: A pin that walks out here is easy to lose and stops the bolt stop working. Look for it before you start cleaning.
deepSteps.aside: The firearm is completely stripped; the parts that may require careful checking and cleaning are now separate.
deepSteps.quote: Make sure that the fastening pin on the bolt stop remains in position once the upper receiver has been separated.
deepSteps.cite: Use • Maintenance — Benelli bolt-action rifle (served by Benelli USA as the Lupo manual, listed for the Lupo HPR) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Stripping procedure, note and close, p.28
deepSteps.warn: the warranty will become null and void in case of tampering or improper stripping by the user.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Routine cleaning of the bore after use
Clean from the breech with the bolt out

cleaning.name: BOLT UNIT
tasks: Bolt unit stripped, cleaned and lubricated
Powder residue wiped from the bolt body, the bolt cap and the striker unit

cleaning.name: TRIGGER GROUP & MAGAZINE
tasks: Powder residue and foreign bodies cleared from the trigger group
Trigger group cleaned as an assembly; the book gives no further strip

cleaning.name: STOCK, FORE-END & EXTERNAL
tasks: Light oil on the parts exposed to the elements — Benelli oil is supplied
Stock and fore-end cleaned with products made for their finish
Do not let oils containing solvents or chemicals reach the stock or fore-end

reassembly: Trigger group, with the safety in the OFF position, into its housing on the bottom of the upper receiver; its screws to 1.2 Nm.
Upper receiver onto the chassis, held pressed down onto the recoil-lug insert.
Two upper receiver screws tightened front first, then back, then tightened again in the same order — 8 Nm.
Magazine into its housing in the chassis.
Firing pin group into the bolt cap.
Bolt cap into the bolt unit with the marks on the two parts aligned; compress the spring while pressing the side button, then turn the cap counterclockwise. A firm surface to push against helps.
Bolt unit into the upper receiver guides, facing the correct direction. With a medium or high comb, turn the bolt 180° from its closed position to get it past the comb.
fncheck: With the rifle proven empty and the muzzle in a safe direction: slide the safety back and confirm the red dot on the upper receiver disappears, then forward so it shows. Turn the bolt with the lever and close it again, and check that the red dot on the cocking piece at the end of the upper receiver is visible — that is how Benelli shows the rifle is cocked. Work the bolt through its full travel and confirm it closes. If your rifle has a bolt locking lever, confirm the bolt stays locked closed with the safety on. ⚠ Benelli asks you to check that the action screws are correctly tightened, especially after the first shots.
